files.lesson.md: --- order: 27 unit: rates node: AC9M8M05 n1 uses: [AC9M7N08 n1] title: Rates summary: "A rate compares two quantities with different units: 60 km per hour, $4 per kg, 80 beats per minute. The unit rate is how much for 1 of the second quantity: divide the first by the second. A ratio compares quantities in the same units. Speeds convert with 1 km/h = 1000 m ÷ 3600 s." language: maths connection: unit-pricing # data/connections/maths.yml voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Speed limits, the price of petrol, your heart rate and how fast your phone downloads: all rates. Each one says 'this much per one of that'." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8318 url: http://127.0.0.1:8318/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: rate.yml#explain-pic, caption: "At 60 km per hour, 2.5 hours matches 150 km: each hour adds another 60 km." } explainClip: query: { code: "@rate.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Per one hour" say: "A rate says how much for one." clip: - caption: { text: "60 km per hour: 1 hour matches 60 km.", say: "Sixty kilometres per hour. One hour matches sixty kilometres." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Each extra hour adds another 60 km.", say: "Each extra hour adds another sixty." } - click: Make the time bigger - click: Make the time bigger - click: Make the time bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "150 km" } - wait: 1500 --- A **rate** compares two quantities measured in **different units**: 60 km per hour (km/h), $4.50 per kilogram ($/kg), 80 beats per minute. A **ratio** compares quantities in the **same** units: 2 cups of flour to 3 cups of milk, 2 : 3. The **unit rate** is the amount for **one** of the second quantity. Divide the first by the second, and keep the units: $$120 \text{ km in } 2.5 \text{ h} \;\Rightarrow\; 120 \div 2.5 = 48 \text{ km per h}$$ Rates convert like units. For speed: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s, so $54 \text{ km/h} = 54 \times 1000 \div 3600 = 15 \text{ m/s}$ (divide by 3.6). ## Predict: a car's speed ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a speed from a distance and a time shows whether they divide distance by time, and keep the units." check: type: predict q: "A car travels 150 km in 2 hours at a steady speed. How far does it go in 1 hour?" options: ["75 km", "300 km", "152 km", "2/150 km"] actual: "75 km: 150 ÷ 2 = 75. The car's speed is 75 km per hour." ``` ## Run: set the rate ```step stage: run insight: "Matching a rate to a distance and time on the double number line shows the unit rate as 'one hour's worth'." try: { playground: board, starter: "rate.yml#run", height: 520 } check: { type: board, text: "Set the rate and the time so that 2 hours matches 150 km. Was your prediction right?", when: "r = 75 and x = 2", explain: "75 km per hour × 2 h = 150 km." } ``` The top line is the distance, the bottom line the time. The dashed line marks 1 hour. ## Investigate: rate or ratio ```step stage: investigate insight: "Rates have two different units, ratios one; the unit rate divides in the right order (Mia divides the wrong way); speeds convert by × 1000 ÷ 3600." tasks: - check: type: sort q: "Rate or ratio?" options: ["Rate", "Ratio"] items: - ["60 km per hour", "Rate"] - ["$3.50 per kg", "Rate"] - ["2 : 3 cordial to water", "Ratio"] - ["80 beats per minute", "Rate"] - ["3 boys to 4 girls", "Ratio"] - ["7 L per 100 km", "Rate"] explain: "A rate has two different units; a ratio compares the same kind of thing." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia works out the price of apples per kilogram. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: rate-inverted explain: "Line 2: dollars per kilogram is dollars ÷ kilograms: 12 ÷ 3 = $4 per kg. 3 ÷ 12 = 0.25 kg per dollar, a different rate." - check: type: number q: "Convert 90 km/h to metres per second." answer: 25 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["324", "That multiplies by 3.6. Metres per second is the smaller number: divide by 3.6."] explain: "90 × 1000 = 90 000 m in 3600 s: 90 000 ÷ 3600 = 25 m/s." ``` ### Rate or ratio Here is the routine. ```worked \text{distance} \div \text{time} :: Divide what you want "per" by the "one" quantity. 150 \div 2.5 = 60 :: 150 km in 2.5 h. 60 \text{ km/h} :: Keep both units in the answer. 60 \div 3.6 \approx 16.7 \text{ m/s} :: To convert km/h to m/s, × 1000 ÷ 3600, which is ÷ 3.6. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working. Dollars per kilogram: which number goes first? ### Convert a speed ## Modify: convert and compare ```step stage: modify insight: "Converting speeds and prices and comparing two rates with the same unit shows unit rates make comparisons fair." try: { playground: board, starter: "rate.yml#free", height: 520 } tasks: - starter: "rate.yml#free" hint: ["The board shows m/s in its notes.", "25 m/s × 3.6 = 90 km/h."] check: { type: board, text: "Set the rate r (in km/h) so the speed is 25 m/s.", when: "m = 25", explain: "25 m/s = 25 × 3.6 = 90 km/h." } - check: type: number q: "Cheese costs $0.80 per 100 g. What is that in dollars per kilogram?" answer: 8 tolerance: 0 explain: "1 kg = 1000 g = 10 × 100 g: $0.80 × 10 = $8 per kg." - check: type: question q: "Rice: 600 g for $4.80, or 1 kg for $7.50. Which is the better buy?" options: ["The 1 kg bag: $7.50 per kg, against $8.00 per kg", "The 600 g bag: it costs less", "They are the same", "You cannot tell without more information"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "It costs less, but you get less: compare per kg.", "$4.80 ÷ 0.6 = $8.00 per kg.", "Unit rates make it fair."] explain: "4.80 ÷ 0.6 = $8.00 per kg, so 1 kg for $7.50 is cheaper per kilogram." - check: type: question q: "Your heart beats 18 times in 15 seconds. What is that in beats per minute?" options: ["72", "18", "33", "270"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is per 15 seconds.", "That adds the numbers.", "That multiplies 18 by 15."] explain: "A minute is 4 lots of 15 seconds: 18 × 4 = 72 beats per minute." ``` ### m/s to km/h ### Price per kilogram ### Best buy ### Heart rate ## Practise: rates ```step stage: practise insight: "Unit rates, conversions and rate or ratio, mixed; dividing the wrong way is the planted slip; the simplest-ratio review keeps ratios separate from rates." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A train travels 240 km in 3 hours. What is its speed in km per hour?" answer: 80 tolerance: 0 explain: "240 ÷ 3 = 80 km/h." - check: type: number q: "Convert 36 km/h to metres per second." answer: 10 tolerance: 0 explain: "36 ÷ 3.6 = 10 m/s." - check: type: number q: "A 2 kg bag of flour costs $3.40. What is the price in dollars per kilogram?" answer: 1.7 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["0.59", "That is kilograms per dollar. Dollars per kilogram: 3.40 ÷ 2."] explain: "3.40 ÷ 2 = $1.70 per kg." smaller: check: { type: question, q: "'Per kilogram' means for each 1 kg. Which division gives that?", options: ["Dollars ÷ kilograms", "Kilograms ÷ dollars"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "That gives kilograms for each dollar. The thing that comes after 'per' is the one you divide by."], explain: "The amount after 'per' goes second: dollars ÷ kilograms." } - check: type: question q: "Review: what is the ratio 12 : 18 in simplest form?" options: ["2 : 3", "3 : 2", "6 : 9", "12 : 18 is already simplest"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The order matters: 12 first.", "6 : 9 can be simplified further.", "Both divide by 6."] explain: "Divide both by 6: 2 : 3." ``` ### Speed ### Convert ### Price per kg ### Review: ratios ## Make: a long drive ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing the rate and the time to match a distance makes students use the unit rate both ways." try: { playground: board, starter: "rate.yml#free", height: 520 } hint: ["280 ÷ 3.5 = ?", "The time is 3 and a half hours."] check: { type: board, text: "A drive covers 280 km in 3.5 hours at a steady speed. Set the rate and the time to match.", when: "r = 80 and x = 3.5", explain: "280 ÷ 3.5 = 80 km/h." } ``` Then give the speed in metres per second, to 1 decimal place. ## Make: the better buy, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A fair comparison needs the same 'per'. The paper task makes them find a unit price for each pack and pick the right division." hint: ["Turn both packs into dollars per 100 g.", "Divide dollars by the number of 100 g lots."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Two packs of the same cereal: 500 g for \\$4.80, or 750 g for \\$6.60. What is the price per 100 g of the better value pack, in dollars?" steps: - ["500 g is five lots of 100 g: $4.80 \\div 5 = 0.96$ dollars per 100 g", "dollars divided by the number of 100 g lots"] - ["750 g is 7.5 lots of 100 g: $6.60 \\div 7.5 = 0.88$ dollars per 100 g", "the same division for the bigger pack"] - ["$0.88 < 0.96$, so the 750 g pack is cheaper per 100 g", "the lower unit price is the better value"] - ["Check: $0.88 \\times 7.5 = 6.60$", "multiplying back gets the pack price"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why compare the unit prices and not the pack prices?" options: - "The packs hold different amounts, so only the price per 100 g compares them fairly" - "The cheaper pack price is always the better value" - "The bigger pack is always the better value" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The \\$4.80 pack costs less but you get less cereal. Put both on the same 'per'.", "Not always: it depends on the prices. Work out the unit prices."] answer: "0.88" answerLabel: "Price per 100 g of the better pack ($)" tolerance: 0.005 feedback: - ["0.96", "That is the smaller pack's price per 100 g. Which pack is cheaper per 100 g?"] - ["6.6", "That is the bigger pack's price, not the price per 100 g. Divide by 7.5."] - ["1.14", "That is 7.5 ÷ 6.60 turned upside down. Dollars go first: 6.60 ÷ 7.5."] criteria: - "I put both packs on the same 'per' before comparing." - "I divided dollars by the number of 100 g lots, not the other way round." - "I said which pack is better value, and checked by multiplying back." explain: "500 g pack: \\$4.80 ÷ 5 = \\$0.96 per 100 g. 750 g pack: \\$6.60 ÷ 7.5 = \\$0.88 per 100 g. The 750 g pack is better value, if you will finish it before it goes stale." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The prices are made up for the task, but supermarket shelf labels show the same unit price. Find a price per 100 g for each pack, compare, and type the lower price. **Also used in** - **Shelf labels.** The 'per 100 g' or 'per kg' price printed under each product is a unit rate worked out for you. - **Petrol.** Litres per 100 km tells you which car costs less to run, because every car is compared on the same distance. - **Heart rate.** Beats counted in 15 seconds become beats per minute by scaling to one minute. ```teacher summary: Students match rates to distances and times on a double number line, tell rates from ratios, find unit rates and convert between rate units such as km/h and m/s (AC9M8M05, node 1). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can write a rate with its two units. - I can find a unit rate by dividing in the right order. - I can convert a speed between km/h and m/s, and tell a rate from a ratio. struggle: "Dividing in the right order. Ask students to say the rate in words ('dollars per kilogram') before they divide: the 'per' quantity goes second." before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need ratios (Number Foundations, Ratios). The one idea: a rate is "this much per one of that", with two different units; divide the first by the second. The common mistake is dividing the wrong way round (Mia's mistake). The board's double number line lines up the two quantities; the dashed line marks the unit rate, and the notes give km/h in m/s. Wider: compare several units for the same speed (km/h, m/s, knots); rates in First Nations land management, such as how fast a cool burn spreads in different conditions (teach with local knowledge where you can). running: - "Predict: ask what '1 hour's worth' is." - "Run: ask what happens to the distance when the time doubles." - "Investigate: ask Mia to say her rate in words." - "Modify: ask why the cheaper bag is not the better buy." - "Make: ask for the speed both ways." - "Paper: the cereal task is worked in books; the page marks the answer ($0.88 per 100 g) and why only unit prices compare fairly. Books out, then look for dollars on top of the division and the same 'per' for both packs." stuck: - see: A student divides the wrong way. ask: What is it per? That goes second. fix: Dollars per kilogram = dollars ÷ kilograms. - see: A student drops the units. ask: 60 what, per what? fix: A rate always has two units. - see: A student multiplies by 3.6 to get m/s. ask: Is a metre per second faster or slower than a kilometre per hour? fix: "m/s is the smaller number: divide by 3.6." stretch: Express the same speed in km/h, m/s and knots (1 knot = 1.852 km/h). Which unit do ships use, and why? support: "A card: 'rate = first quantity ÷ second quantity, units: first per second'." leads: > This starts AC9M8M05. Where it leads: using rates to solve problems (next lesson), rate models, and gradient as a rate (Linear relations). exit: q: A cyclist rides 45 km in 1.5 hours. Find her speed in km/h and m/s. a: 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h; 30 ÷ 3.6 ≈ 8.3 m/s. explain: > A **rate** compares two quantities with **different units** (km per hour, $ per kg); a **ratio** compares the same kind of quantity. The **unit rate** is the amount for one of the second quantity: divide the first by the second, and keep both units. To convert km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6. ```
